FORGEMCP — HAND RIG ANATOMICAL CORRECTION: EXECUTION AND VALIDATION

Milestone ID: FMCP-BLENDER-HAND-ANATOMY-CORRECTION
Status: CORRECTION APPLIED — SAMPLED POSES VERIFIED; CONTINUOUS PLAYBACK NOT VERIFIED
Date: October 30, 2026
Related records: End-to-end rigging, skinning and animation milestone; finger-flexion issue; anatomical correction milestone proposal; future webcam motion-capture proposal.

Executive summary

This report records the execution follow-up to the October 30 hand-rigging milestone. The initial v002 animation made the four fingers bend backward. Inspection of its Action and the live rig showed that the deforming skeleton, skin weights and armature binding were present; the problematic values were the finger flexion animation rotations. A controlled pose check showed that the Action's positive local-X flexion values moved the tested index chain in the wrong direction. Reversing those values on a new versioned copy made the digits curl toward the palm in the sampled poses. The armature rest bones, parent hierarchy, mesh geometry and weights were left unchanged.

The correction is saved as Hand_Rig_Animation_Final_20261030_v003_AnatomicalCorrection.blend. The v002 baseline was restored byte-for-byte from its original .blend1 after a separate copy of the corrected state was retained. Independent Blender 5.2.3 background readbacks opened both files: v002 retained its original Action, while v003 contained Hand_Demo_Animation.004 with the corrected finger curves. v003 still has a 22-bone armature, the original 9,584-vertex rigged mesh, the armature modifier, and all 9,584 vertices weighted with normalized sums.

At sampled frames, the index, middle, ring and pinky each curled independently; the thumb articulated on its distinct existing axes; frames 88 and 100 showed combined/partial curls; frame 108 produced a stronger closed-hand pose; and frame 120 returned to neutral. Actual evaluated mesh readback showed deformation at those poses and neutral geometry within roughly 1 × 10⁻⁷ world units of the source. Viewport captures of the closed pose were inspected from current, right and three-quarter views without an obvious collapse or crossing. This is meaningful evidence for the correction, but it does not close all visual acceptance criteria.

Continuous timeline playback of v003 remains NOT VERIFIED. The native computer-control pipe was unavailable, so the corrected file could not be played through the complete timeline in the UI. The open Blender session also continued to report the v002 path while its in-memory Action contained the correction. The corrected disk artifact is v003; saving from that stale live session to v002 could overwrite the restored baseline. Reopen v003 before saving any further edits.

Baseline and diagnosis

The target was the existing Hand_Rig_Animation_Final_20261030_v002.blend scene. It contains the original mesh tripo_node_2038746d, a rigged copy tripo_node_2038746d_Rigged, and armature Hand_Rig_Reconstructed. The rig has 22 bones, including 21 deform bones. The rigged mesh has 9,584 vertices and 19,175 polygons, with one Armature modifier targeting that armature. The file's Hand_Demo_Animation Action contains 57 pose-bone Euler-rotation curves and 855 keys over frames 1–120 at 24 frames per second.

The Action used positive local-X values for flexion on Index, Middle, Ring and Pinky. A controlled index test at frame 12 established that the existing positive sign bent away from the intended palm curl; reversing the three tested chain rotations moved the fingertip and visible finger toward the palm. Repeating the same sign interpretation against the other three finger chains produced the same direction. The diagnosis is therefore specific: the four-finger local-X flexion key values had the wrong sign relative to the existing bone-local bases and intended motion.

The thumb was not assigned the four-finger X rule. Its saved articulation uses different channels: metacarpal X and proximal/distal Z. Its existing articulation was preserved during the single-finger correction. A stronger thumb contribution was added only at the combined close pose. No bone roll, rest orientation, bone position, parenting, weight, modifier, vertex, UV, material or source-mesh data was changed.

Changes on the versioned copy

The four fingers each have three animated phalanges and four established pose keys. The 48 nonzero local-X finger flexion values were sign-reversed in the copied Action. This keeps the skeleton and deformation system intact while changing the smallest identified cause. The corrected Action was copied into a new Action datablock rather than replacing the original baseline Action.

A stronger combined pose was authored at frame 108 on v003: the four-finger Proximal/Middle/Distal local-X values are −0.9/−1.2/−0.7 radians. The thumb contribution is Metacarpal X −0.55, Proximal Z −0.75, and Distal Z −0.5 radians. Frames 88 and 100 retain partial-curl values. The action returns to neutral by frame 120. These values describe this hand's existing local coordinate system; they are not a reusable universal hand-axis convention.

Verification matrix

Check Evidence Status

Corrected artifact v003 independently opened in Blender 5.2.3; SHA-256 2D07C1501A8EED13F3B9421BD4F94D12AD9D2B56965483C2A5F14F110373E084 PASS
Finger Action channels 57 curves remain; individual-chain local-X values are negative in the corrected poses PASS
Independent fingers Index frame 12; middle 27; ring 42; pinky 57. Each target chain changed its mesh region while other single-digit chains were neutral PASS at sampled frames
Thumb Frame 72 evaluated with existing X/Z channels; thumb region deformed PASS at sampled frame
Combined curl Frames 88 and 100 contain multi-digit curls PASS at sampled frames
Strong close pose Frame 108 contains increased four-finger and thumb flexion; viewport captures inspected PASS for sampled pose; not full visual certification
Open/neutral return Frame 78 has open fingers; frame 120 has zero pose rotations and no material evaluated-mesh change PASS at sampled frames
Weight integrity 9,584 of 9,584 vertices weighted; 0 non-normalized vertices; 21,379 assignments remain PASS
Continuous playback Full v003 start-to-end timeline playback could not be controlled in the UI NOT VERIFIED
Exhaustive visual quality Not all front/back/side/palm combinations, all frames, self-intersections or contact stresses were inspected NOT VERIFIED

The evaluated-mesh comparisons are Blender dependency-graph results, not estimates from rotation values alone. Neutral restoration compares the evaluated rigged copy to the matching source geometry and reports only floating-point-scale error. The deformation checks confirm response of the weighted mesh; they do not certify every vertex's surface quality or every intermediate frame.

Artifact and recovery

The corrected version is the v003 filename above. The baseline v002 file now matches its original .blend1 SHA-256. A pre-correction saved copy and a corrected-state snapshot were retained separately during recovery. The separate pre-correction copy was created before edits; its independent reopen was not performed. The v003 file, by contrast, was independently reopened and read back.

The working copy retained the 22-bone armature, 21 deform bones, 9,584 vertices, 19,175 polygons, Armature modifier and normalized weights. The source mesh was not replaced. The separate approximately one-million-triangle master hand was not opened or modified. No retopology, decimation or webcam code was performed.

Remaining acceptance work

The root cause is established and the correction is present in the saved v003 Action, but this report does not claim the complete proposed anatomical milestone has passed. The next verification should:

  1. Open v003 as the active Blender file, then play frames 1–120 continuously and confirm repeatable motion and neutral return.
  2. Inspect neutral, isolated curls, thumb opposition, partial curl and frame-108 close pose in labeled front, back, side and palm views.
  3. Record fingertip paths, joint-axis interpretation, non-target digit movement and wrist/palm stability.
  4. Review mesh contact and intersections at close poses; numerical bounding boxes are not a self-intersection certificate.
  5. Reopen the saved v003 again after any approved follow-up edit and compare action, weights, modifier and neutral geometry.

Until those gates pass, current status is correction applied and sampled poses verified; continuous playback and exhaustive visual acceptance remain unverified. The prototype is not certified as a production control rig, a generalized automatic character-rigging system, or game-engine ready. Auto-Rig Pro did not generate this hand skeleton; this correction retains the existing custom hand rig. Webcam motion capture and MediaPipe integration remain unimplemented future work.

Engineering significance

The result shows why pose-channel interpretation must be checked against the actual mesh and bone-local basis. A rig can have valid skin weights, a correctly targeted Armature modifier and independently responsive finger chains while still producing the wrong anatomical gesture. By diagnosing the sign on the existing Action and changing only the copied finger keys, the correction preserves working geometry and binding while giving the team concrete evidence for future rigging acceptance checks.

The reusable lesson is not that negative X always means finger flexion. It is that flexion direction must be established per skeleton from a labeled neutral hand, then checked in evaluated deformation and visible motion. ForgeMCP's current evidence supports this one custom rig, these saved files and the sampled poses reported here. It does not demonstrate arbitrary hand inference or a universal automatic correction operator.
